title: Elbow-Knee Connection
shortDefinition: Elbow-knee connection closes the space between upper body and hip line to prevent pins and passes.
whyItMatters: When elbow separates from knee, the opponent inserts chest, knee, hook, or arm isolation.
deepExplanation: This is a survival principle in side control, mount, guard retention, and back escape. It rebuilds a defensive layer before shrimping, bridging, or wrestling up.
beginnerView: Bring elbow inside, then bring knee back.
advancedView: Use elbow-knee to bait pressure then switch to underhook, turtle, or guard recovery.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Elbow-Knee Connection during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Elbow-Knee Connection to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Elbow-Knee Connection is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Elbow-Knee Connection before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
